title: Thiou Boulettes, Fish Balls in Vegetable Sauce
author: Sophie
desc: White-fish balls bound with cornflour and peanut butter, fried golden, then warmed on a tomato sauce and a pot of potato, sweet potato, carrot and cabbage.
longDesc: A home-cook version from La Tendresse en Cuisine: 600 g of white fish (pollock) minced with an egg, onion, garlic, a spoon of peanut butter, harissa standing in for the chile, and a spoon of cornflour, fried until golden all over. The sauce is tomato, concentrate, onion and garlic with the oil from the boulettes; the vegetables cook about an hour, stirred every quarter of an hour, then the sauce is blended to a thick consistency. The fish balls rest on the vegetables ten minutes to warm through.
ingredients: 600 g white fish fillets (the cook used pollock)
1 level tbsp harissa (used in place of chile)
Neutral oil for frying — quantity not printed
3 tbsp of the frying oil from the fish balls
equipment: Immersion blender or blender for the sauce
steps: Process the fish with the egg, onion, garlic, peanut butter, harissa, pepper, salt and cornflour into a paste with no visible pieces.
Shape into balls and fry in neutral oil until well golden on every side. Keep the frying oil.
For the sauce, cook the tomatoes, concentrate, onion, garlic, pepper and harissa in 3 tablespoons of the frying oil.
Add the potato, cabbage, carrot and sweet potato with water as needed and cook about 1 hour, stirring every quarter hour, until the vegetables are cooked and tender.
Blend part of the pot to make a thick sauce.
Lay the fish balls on the vegetables and warm them for 10 minutes. Season to taste.
chefTips: Process the fish until ‘there are no visible pieces left’ — a smooth paste holds the ball together.
Fry ‘until well golden on all sides’; they finish cooking in the sauce afterwards.
Keep 3 tablespoons of the frying oil; it carries the fish flavour into the sauce.
Harissa is the cook’s substitution for chile, and she says so.
commonMistakes: Leaving fish pieces in the mix so the balls break.
Adding the balls to the pot earlier than the last 10 minutes.
healthBenefits: Four vegetables in the pot give fibre and beta-carotene.
culturalNote: Neither version of thiou boulettes read for this collection ties the dish to Saint-Louis, despite the association made elsewhere; a second printing under a ‘196 flavors’ site byline differs on the fish, the binder and the sauce and is truncated mid-method, so it is not published.
sources: Source: latendresseencuisine.com, ‘Thiou boulettes (Sénégal)’. Byline: ‘Sophie’ (first name only). No publication date printed (metadata 2016-04-03, modified 2024-04-13). Yield: ‘Portions 6 Personnes’. SINGLE-PASS.

SUSPECTED MISPRINT, reported as printed: the header says ‘Temps de préparation 50 minutes’, ‘Temps de cuisson 1 minute’ and ‘Temps total 51 minutes’, while the method itself calls for about an hour of simmering. The cook time here (70) follows the method (about 1 hour plus 10 minutes), not the header.

Cues in short fragments: ‘bien dorées sur toutes les faces’; ‘Quand les légumes sont cuits et tendres’; ‘plus aucun morceau visible’. Origin statement on the page, in full: ‘Le Sénégal a pour capitale Dakar, il se situe sur la côte Atlantique.’

DISAGREEMENT with a second printing (chefsimon.com, ‘196 flavors’ site-name byline, truncated at step 4; the source page is robots-blocked): 1 kg capitaine instead of 600 g pollock; 250 g stale breadcrumb instead of cornflour and peanut butter; 250 ml water and green pepper instead of root vegetables. The two are not variants of one recipe as printed. Only this version is published.
